chapter_mission: Widen the crisis beyond the Corridor, let Torin make the clean-sacrifice case, and show Ben choosing secrecy again even after Luke asks directly.
chapter_turn: Ben sees more of the pattern and still doubles down on handling it alone.

scene_plan.purpose: Let the outpost reports and Luke's message make the crisis feel bigger than the ship.
Use the galley argument to make Torin's answer sound frighteningly reasonable.
In the nook, make the report real enough to hurt when Ben deletes it, and keep Kael and Torin as an unread private moment.

relationship_turns.to: active deception — Ben has now received a direct request for status and elected not to answer. The withholding has moved from editorial discretion to disobedience. He will feel it later; he does not feel it yet
mirrored pattern — Torin has just used Ben's own behaviour as the proof of his argument. Ben cannot dismiss it because Torin is accurate. The tactical alliance holds; the ground under it has moved

relationship_turns.from: the Lie operating in the background
relationship_turns.to: the Lie recognised and chosen — Ben sees the Gavran pattern in himself and commits to it one more day. Recognition is not yet change. The book's engine runs on the gap
private conversation Ben does not hear — the shape of a relationship Ben has no access to. Not plot; texture. Per W1 and D7 guardrails, the beat is a sentence or two and is not underlined.

exit_vector: Ship in transit toward the intercept point. Ben's datapad holding a deleted full report and an unanswered coded message from Luke. Torin's observation sitting in the space between Ben and the work surface he is not using. Sera three compartments away, silent — still defending him to herself. Kael in his bunk, whatever he and Torin spoke of unspoken. The institutional question subplot at its deepest point; the Jacen-parallel recognition now fully available for when Ben chooses to use it (per R13, the explicit naming waits for Ch 18).
notes: This chapter should feel like the outside galaxy pressing in. Torin's argument needs warmth and force, and Ben's deleted report should feel like a worse choice because it is fully informed.
